name: paulweaver34
about: Christian. Grantmaker. 20 years in Istanbul. Philosophy → MPA → Grant Making → Bitcoin & AI. Writing about where trust lives — and what happens when it moves.

releases.title: How Good People Drift into Disaster
releases.summary: The smallest cluster and the sharpest. Six essays using popular culture the way a theologian uses a parable. Girard's mimetic desire runs beneath every system. 'The Choices We Call Necessity' — the Devil Wears Prada essay — is the sharpest piece in the corpus: Hannah Arendt meets Miranda Priestly, and the argument is that moral drift doesn't announce itself. You just stop noticing what you're becoming.

releases.title: The Artifacts of a Life
releases.summary: The biographical essays are where the intellectual framework becomes flesh. A 256MB JumpDrive becomes a meditation on SHA-256. A Grameen Bank cost-benefit analysis becomes a reckoning with Banfield's radius of trust. Standing in the rubble of Antakya six days after the earthquake. The Joe Wendel funeral essay using 'proof of work' as a metaphor for what you build invisibly over time.

releases.title: Institutions — 21 Essays on Trust and Its Architecture
releases.summary: Twenty-five minutes. Twenty-one essays. The question underneath all of them: what happens to institutions when trust migrates to protocols? Bitcoin, Ottoman history, Girard, Banfield — the whole radius-of-trust argument in audio form.

releases.title: Money, Desire, and Honest Weights — 21 Essays
releases.summary: Twenty-two minutes. Twenty-one essays. From Abraham’s silver weights at Machpelah to Nixon’s 1971 gold window closure to Bitcoin’s fixed supply — the moral case for sound money is older than any central bank. Girard, Banfield, Leviticus, and the Federal Reserve in the same conversation.

releases.title: Faith as a Way of Knowing
releases.summary: Not devotional writing — epistemology with a pulse. Plantinga's 'warrant' and 'proper function' run beneath all of it. The Abraham diptych (Genesis 22 and 23) is the center of gravity. Kierkegaard's Johannes de Silentio gives listener a vocabulary for the kind of trust that cannot be explained from the outside. Faith is not opposed to reason — it is a specific form of knowing that reason alone cannot replicate.

releases.title: AI & the Architecture of Attention
releases.summary: Nine essays circling a single anxiety: what happens to human knowing when the tools for knowing become autonomous? From prediction markets and moral hazard, through the oracle problem, to AI as coroner rather than killer. The final essay — uploading Kierkegaard to an AI and discovering the machine asked something he hadn't thought to ask himself. The conclusion: AI is not the threat. Formation is the issue.

releases.title: A world where generosity flows freely across borders, and where Christian communities have the tools they need to endure
releases.summary: A world where generosity flows freely across borders, and where Christian communities have the tools they need to endure, serve, and flourish.
